home_content_block_body:
Most of our work as a landscaper in Southampton takes us across a city where no two gardens are quite the same. In Bassett Heath, we work on large detached plots along roads like Saxholm Way and Pinehurst Road, where long, narrow gardens and mature trees mean the layout has to work around established root systems, not just planting plans. In Portswood, gardens on the conservation estate built between 1908 and 1930 come with generous frontages and genuine character, but paving and boundary changes there call for careful thought, because Article 4 controls mean the front garden layout carries more weight than it would on a newer street.\n\nWe are a four-person, family run team and we have completed over 100 jobs across the city. Our [landscape gardener](/landscape-gardener/) work covers the design and build end of the garden, and our [landscape designer](/landscape-designer/) service is there when you want a drawn scheme before anything goes in the ground. For regular visits, our [gardener](/gardener/) service handles maintenance on an ongoing basis, and our [lawn care service](/lawn-care-service/) is built around the lawn itself, whether that is turfing, feeding or getting a neglected lawn back to shape.\n\nOne concern we hear often is about prices shifting once the job is underway. We price the full job before we start and we do not add to it. Another is whether the groundwork will hold. We take drainage and levels seriously on every hard landscaping job, because a patio that holds water or a path that sinks is a problem that comes back.\n\nWe cover Southampton and nearby towns including [landscaping in Romsey](/locations/romsey/), [landscaping in Winchester](/locations/winchester/), and [landscaping in Chandlers Ford](/locations/chandlers-ford/), and everywhere in between. Call [CV: phone] to talk through what you have in mind.

Edens Edge Landscaping handles gardens from the ground up, covering hard landscaping, lawn and planting work, tree care, and regular maintenance for homeowners across Southampton and the surrounding towns.

  - card_name: Paving contractor | card_text: Patios, driveways and paths that are laid right hold their shape for years. As your [paving contractor](/paving-contractor/), we carry out the full job: base preparation, falls for drainage, and surface laying across a range of materials. Getting the ground underneath right is where most paving jobs either succeed or fail.

Our [deck builder](/deck-builder/) team handles everything from the subframe to the finished boards, and we match the height, material and finish to the garden around it so the deck sits properly rather than looking like an afterthought.

home_faq_items:
  - faq_question: How much does landscaping cost in Southampton? | faq_answer: It depends on the job, and the honest answer is that the range is wide. A straightforward lawn replacement costs significantly less than a full garden redesign with hard landscaping. The main factors are garden size, how much groundwork is needed, the materials chosen and whether access is straightforward or constrained. Call [CV: phone] or send us a message and we will tell you what affects the price for the specific job you have in mind.
  - faq_question: Are you insured? | faq_answer: Yes. We carry public liability cover up to £5m. That cover applies while we are on site and is there for situations like accidental damage to your property or injury to a third party during the work. It covers the kind of incidents that can happen on any landscaping job, from a stone slipping during paving work to a branch coming down in the wrong place during a tree job.
  - faq_question: What happens if something isn't right after the job? | faq_answer: Call us and we will come back to look at it. Every job we carry out is done to a reasonable standard of care and skill, and if something is not right we want to know about it. We do not expect you to live with a problem. The straightforward approach is to get in touch as soon as you notice something and we will work out what needs to happen next.
  - faq_question: How soon can you start? | faq_answer: We can usually make a start within the same week for smaller jobs. Larger projects that need more planning or materials to be ordered are typically booked a little further ahead. When we give you a quote, we will confirm a realistic start date at the same time so you are not left waiting for an answer.
  - faq_question: Is the quote free and no obligation? | faq_answer: Yes, the quote is free and there is no obligation to go ahead. We come out, look at the garden and give you a fixed price. If it is not the right time or you decide to go a different way, that is fine.
  - faq_question: Which areas do you cover? | faq_answer: We cover Southampton and the towns around it, including [Romsey](/locations/romsey/), [Chandlers Ford](/locations/chandlers-ford/), [Eastleigh](/locations/eastleigh/), [Winchester](/locations/winchester/), [Totton](/locations/totton/), [Hedge End](/locations/hedge-end/) and [West End](/locations/west-end/), among others. We travel up to 20 miles from Southampton, so if you are not sure whether we reach you, just ask.
  - faq_question: How long does a garden landscaping project take? | faq_answer: It depends on what is involved. A new lawn or a single border redesign can be done in a day or two. A full garden build with paving, fencing, planting and drainage could run to one or two weeks depending on size and access. Hard landscaping days can also be moved by weather, particularly when laying paving or carrying out groundwork in wet conditions. We give you a realistic timeframe when we price the job.
  - faq_question: Why does water sit on my patio or lawn after rain? | faq_answer: Persistent waterlogging usually comes from more than one thing at once. The three most common causes are ground that drains slowly beneath the surface, a paved or laid surface with falls that send water the wrong way, and no drain or soakaway to take water away once it arrives. In Southampton, the picture is complicated by genuinely varied ground conditions: slower-draining, seasonally waterlogged soils have been recorded at investigated sites across the city, and gardens close to the rivers and reclaimed land near the waterfront can sit above ground that holds water at depth. A permeable surface helps, but it does not resolve the problem if the ground beneath it cannot absorb the water quickly enough. The fix depends on which of these is driving the issue, and that is something we can assess when we visit.
